topic: npm-scan: Modern Supply Chain Security for the npm Ecosystem 2026

key_points: Open-source npm supply chain scanner with 23 behavioral detectors
Detects obfuscated payloads, credential stealers, kernel rootkits, eBPF hooks, memory extraction, GitHub spoofing, AI-targeted attacks
95%+ detection on real campaigns (IronWorm, Miasma, Dependency Confusion)
Runs locally — no telemetry, no cloud dependency
Policy-as-code with YAML allowlists and severity overrides
SBOM + SARIF output (CycloneDX, SPDX, GitHub Security)
VINCE integration for CISA reporting
GitHub Action, Docker, CI/CD ready
Free MIT for OSS/individuals, paid BLA for commercial production
Traditional CVE/dependency-version based approach
Covers dependency confusion attacks, malicious backdoors, build pipeline compromise
2818 maintainer emails on expired domains could hijack 8,494 packages
58.7% of packages and 44.3% of maintainers inactive in npm registry
Average npm package trusts 79 third-party packages and 39 maintainers

Behavioral detection approach — catches malicious behavior, not just CVEs

angles: Traditional tools (npm audit, Snyk) are CVE-based and miss 95%+ of behavioral attacks — npm-scan fills this critical gap
The 2026 attack wave includes eBPF kernel rootkits, AI token targeting, GitHub author spoofing, and worm-like propagation — none detectable by legacy tools
Cost-benefit analysis: $2.4K/year for npm-scan enterprise vs $4.5M average data breach = 1,875x ROI
Compliance implications: single-tool approach creates blind spots that auditors will flag under SOC 2 and GDPR
npm-scan is open source (MIT) for individuals/OSS with commercial licensing — lowers barrier to adoption
VINCE integration enables direct CISA reporting — unique among npm security tools
The September 2025 attack proved that detection latency matters: organizations with unified visibility responded effectively, the rest scrambled
Behavioral detection is the new standard — 192,742 malicious packages in 2025 carry no CVE identifiers and are invisible to traditional scanners
